author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Vita Beata (On the Happy Life)
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
